labs.risk.var.explain.parametricText: VaR = V·(z·σ_h − μ_h); fast to compute but assumes normality, underestimating tail risk.
labs.risk.var.explain.historicalText: Uses the empirical quantile of historical returns—distribution-free but sample-dependent (here a Student-t distribution simulates fat tails).
labs.risk.var.explain.monteCarloText: Simulates random paths; flexible but computationally intensive.
labs.risk.var.explain.esText: The average loss beyond VaR; satisfies subadditivity and is more robust than VaR.
labs.risk.var.chart.title: Monte Carlo Loss Distribution and VaR Threshold
labs.risk.var.chart.footnote: The red region marks tail losses exceeding the Monte Carlo VaR. Fat-tailed historical simulation VaR/ES is typically higher than the normal parametric method, highlighting how the normality assumption understates tail risk.
